o1.biggest_strength: It makes the right strategic call: do not cut to 20%, because referred customers are better customers and the real problems are lost credit, slow payouts, and the top 20 partners feeling ignored.
o1.biggest_mistake: Some of the projection math around the 90-day window and the year-one savings from cutting only new referrals is a bit hand-wavy and would need finance to check before we publish it internally.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the cost model for the 90-day window, simplify a few numbers, and turn the first-30-days table into the exact operating checklist for the partner manager.

o2.biggest_strength: It is very clear and gets the main answer right: the 20% cut is risky, the top 20 matter most, and the 30-day credit window is unfair to partners like Kwame.
o2.biggest_mistake: It adds a 40% first-year Partner tier even though the data says payout speed and attribution are the real complaints, and the cost estimate for that tier is not strong enough for a finance conversation.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Keep the 30% rate, make the Partner tier about service, speed, attribution, and co-marketing, and sharpen the cost controls around the bonus and free account ideas.

reason: I would rather hand Output 1 to the team tomorrow because it fixes the real leaks without creating a new commission-cost problem. Output 2 is strong, but the 40% Partner tier feels like an unnecessary answer to a problem the data did not show.
